descriptor: Comprehensive React library + MUI X data components

sections.overview:
### Overview
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/all-components/

MUI (Material UI) is a React component library that implements Google's **Material Design**. It is fully **theme-driven**: a single `theme` object created with `createTheme()` cascades to every component, and per-instance overrides are applied inline via the `sx` prop. The theme root exposes `palette`, `typography`, `spacing`, `shape`, `shadows` (Array of 25), `breakpoints`, `zIndex`, `transitions`, `mixins`, and `components`.

### Packages
- **@mui/material**: the Material Design component set (Inputs, Data display, Feedback, Surfaces, Navigation, Layout).
- **MUI X**: advanced data components — Data Grid, Charts, Date/Time Pickers, Tree View (open-core: Community MIT + Pro/Premium commercial).
- **@mui/icons-material**: 2,100+ Material icons as React components.

### Component inventory (@mui/material)
Organized into categories on the all-components page:
- **Inputs**: Autocomplete, Button, Button Group, Checkbox, Floating Action Button, Radio Group, Rating, Select, Slider, Switch, Text Field, Transfer List, Toggle Button.
- **Data display**: Avatar, Badge, Chip, Divider, Icons, Material Icons, List, Table, Tooltip, Typography.
- **Feedback**: Alert, Backdrop, Dialog, Progress, Skeleton, Snackbar.
- **Surfaces**: Accordion, App Bar, Card, Paper.
- **Navigation**: Bottom Navigation, Breadcrumbs, Drawer, Link, Menu, Pagination, Speed Dial, Stepper, Tabs.
- **Layout**: Box, Container, Grid, Stack, Image List.
- **Lab**: Masonry, Timeline.
- **Utils**: Click-Away Listener, CSS Baseline, Modal, No SSR, Popover, Popper, Portal, Textarea Autosize, Transitions, useMediaQuery.

### Known gaps
MUI notes it follows Material Design "where practical" and does not implement every spec exactly; several components carry a "No guidelines" label (no Material Design guideline reference).
sections.colors:
### Colors
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/palette/

Palette colors live under `theme.palette.*`. Each palette color is represented by four tokens:
- **main** (`theme.palette.<color>.main`): the main shade of the color.
- **light** (`theme.palette.<color>.light`): a lighter shade of `main`.
- **dark** (`theme.palette.<color>.dark`): a darker shade of `main`.
- **contrastText** (`theme.palette.<color>.contrastText`): text color intended to contrast with `main`.

Mode is set via `palette.mode: 'light' | 'dark'`. Built-in light/dark color schemes can be enabled with `colorSchemes: { light: true, dark: true }`. `light`/`dark` are derived from `main` using `tonalOffset` (default `0.2`); `contrastText` is derived using `contrastThreshold` (default `3`, i.e. min 3:1). Setting `contrastThreshold: 4.5` targets WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3.

### Default palette values (light mode)
| Token | light | main | dark |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| primary | `#42a5f5` | `#1976d2` | `#1565c0` |
| secondary | `#ba68c8` | `#9c27b0` | `#7b1fa2` |
| error | `#ef5350` | `#d32f2f` | `#c62828` |
| warning | `#ff9800` | `#ed6c02` | `#e65100` |
| info | `#03a9f4` | `#0288d1` | `#01579b` |
| success | `#4caf50` | `#2e7d32` | `#1b5e20` |

`primary.contrastText` defaults to `#fff`. For other palette colors `contrastText` is auto-calculated against `contrastThreshold` unless overridden. The default secondary palette uses the `A`-prefixed accent shades; the others use un-prefixed shades.

### Purpose
- **primary**: primary interface elements.
- **secondary**: secondary interface elements.
- **error**: elements the user should be made aware of.
- **warning**: potentially dangerous actions or important messages.
- **info**: highlighting neutral information.
- **success**: successful completion of a user-triggered action.

### Not published
Exact dark-mode palette hex values are computed from the same tokens and are not listed as a static table on the palette page (explore via the theme viewer / `window.theme.palette`).
sections.typography:
### Typography
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/typography/ · https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/default-theme/

Typography lives under `theme.typography`. The default font family is **Roboto** (`"Roboto","Helvetica","Arial",sans-serif`). Sizes use `rem` units so they respect the user's browser root font size; `htmlFontSize` defaults to `16`, and `typography.fontSize` (base) defaults to `14`. The `responsiveFontSizes()` helper makes variants scale across breakpoints.

### Variants (13 by default)
`h1`–`h6`, `subtitle1`, `subtitle2`, `body1`, `body2`, `button`, `caption`, `overline`. Each maps directly to generated CSS and can be overridden individually; custom variants can be added and defaults disabled.

### Default variant values
| Variant | Weight | Size (rem) | Line height |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| h1 | 300 | 6 | 1.167 |
| h2 | 300 | 3.75 | 1.2 |
| h3 | 400 | 3 | 1.167 |
| h4 | 400 | 2.125 | 1.235 |
| h5 | 400 | 1.5 | 1.334 |
| h6 | 500 | 1.25 | 1.6 |
| subtitle1 | 400 | 1 | 1.75 |
| subtitle2 | 500 | 0.875 | 1.57 |
| body1 | 400 | 1 | 1.5 |
| body2 | 400 | 0.875 | 1.43 |
| button | 500 | 0.875 | 1.75 (uppercase) |
| caption | 400 | 0.75 | 1.66 |
| overline | 400 | 0.75 | 2.66 (uppercase) |

### Font weights
`fontWeightLight` 300, `fontWeightRegular` 400, `fontWeightMedium` 500, `fontWeightBold` 700.

### Not published
The typography customization page describes variants and overrides; the numeric defaults above come from the default theme object (viewable via the theme viewer / `window.theme.typography`).
sections.layout:
### Layout
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/spacing/

Spacing is generated by the `theme.spacing()` helper, which uses a recommended **8px** scaling factor by default: `theme.spacing(2)` → `'16px'`. The transform can be customized with a number, a function (e.g. Bootstrap `0.25 * factor rem`), or an array. `spacing()` accepts up to 4 arguments to reduce boilerplate: `theme.spacing(1, 2)` → `'8px 16px'`; string values like `'auto'` are supported.

### Spacing scale (default, factor = 8px)
| `spacing(n)` | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `spacing(0)` | 0px |
| `spacing(0.5)` | 4px |
| `spacing(1)` | 8px |
| `spacing(2)` | 16px |
| `spacing(3)` | 24px |
| `spacing(4)` | 32px |
| `spacing(8)` | 64px |

### Layout primitives
- **Box** (`@mui/material/Box`): generic `sx`-aware container.
- **Stack**: one-dimensional flex layout with token-aware `spacing`.
- **Grid**: responsive grid layout.
- **Container**: centers content with max-width breakpoints.

Responsive behavior is driven by `theme.breakpoints`; the `sx` prop applies token-aware overrides inline.

### Not published
Default breakpoint pixel values are defined on `theme.breakpoints` and not enumerated on the spacing page (see the default theme viewer).
sections.depth:
### Elevation & Depth
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/react-paper/ · https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/default-theme/

MUI implements Material Design's elevation system as `theme.shadows` — an **Array of 25** predefined box-shadow strings (indices `0`–`24`). Index `0` is `none`; higher indices produce stronger shadows, mapping to greater perceived distance from the background. The **Paper** component pulls a shadow from this array via its `elevation` prop, which accepts values from `0` to `24` (default `1`). In dark mode, higher elevation also lightens the surface via a semi-transparent `background-image` gradient overlay.

### Elevation levels and common component defaults
| `elevation` | `theme.shadows[n]` | Typical use (default) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `none` | Flat / `variant="outlined"` surfaces |
| 1 | shadows[1] | Paper / Card (default) |
| 2 | shadows[2] | Low raised surfaces |
| 3 | shadows[3] | — |
| 4 | shadows[4] | App Bar (default) |
| 6 | shadows[6] | Floating action button (resting) |
| 8 | shadows[8] | Menu / Popover |
| 12 | shadows[12] | — |
| 16 | shadows[16] | Drawer (temporary) |
| 24 | shadows[24] | Dialog / Modal |

### Not published
The exact box-shadow CSS strings for each of the 25 levels are generated by `createTheme` and shown in the default theme viewer rather than listed in prose; the shadows page path (`/customization/shadows/`) returns 404 — elevation is documented via Paper and the default theme viewer.
sections.shapes:
### Shapes
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/default-theme/ · https://mui.com/material-ui/react-paper/

Corner rounding is controlled by a single token, **`theme.shape.borderRadius`**, whose default value is **4** (px). Components reference this token and may multiply it for larger surfaces so rounding stays proportional across the system.

- **shape.borderRadius** (`theme.shape.borderRadius`): base radius token — default `4`.

The Paper component has rounded corners by default and accepts a `square` prop to remove them; the `outlined` variant renders a flat, bordered surface with no shadow.

### Not published
`theme.shape` exposes `borderRadius` as its documented radius token; a multi-step radius scale (sm/md/lg) is not defined — components derive rounding from the single value.
sections.iconography:
### Iconography
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/material-icons/

**@mui/icons-material** provides **2,100+** official Material Icons converted to `SvgIcon` React components. Install requires `@mui/icons-material @mui/material @emotion/styled @emotion/react`. The search field supports synonyms (e.g. "hamburger", "logout").

### Themes (5)
Each icon is available in five visual themes:
| Theme | Suffix convention |
| --- | --- |
| Filled | (default, no suffix) |
| Outlined | `Outlined` |
| Rounded | `Rounded` |
| Two tone | `TwoTone` |
| Sharp | `Sharp` |

Icons are rendered through the SvgIcon component, so they inherit `fontSize`, `color`, and theme integration.

### Not published
A single authoritative per-theme icon count is not published; the docs state "2,100+" across the set.
sections.components:
### Components
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/all-components/ · https://mui.com/x/react-data-grid/

Components are theme-driven with variants and states configurable globally (via `theme.components.<MuiComponent>`) or per-instance (via props and `sx`). State styling uses global state classes such as `.Mui-disabled` and `.Mui-focusVisible`.

### Category coverage (@mui/material)
- **Inputs**: Autocomplete, Button, Button Group, Checkbox, FAB, Radio Group, Rating, Select, Slider, Switch, Text Field, Transfer List, Toggle Button.
- **Data display**: Avatar, Badge, Chip, Divider, List, Table, Tooltip, Typography.
- **Feedback**: Alert, Backdrop, Dialog, Progress, Skeleton, Snackbar.
- **Surfaces**: Accordion, App Bar, Card, Paper.
- **Navigation**: Bottom Navigation, Breadcrumbs, Drawer, Link, Menu, Pagination, Speed Dial, Stepper, Tabs.
- **Layout**: Box, Container, Grid, Stack, Image List.

### MUI X data components
- **Data Grid** (`@mui/x-data-grid`): sorting, filtering, pagination, editing built in (Community, MIT). **DataGridPro** adds advanced filtering, column pinning, column/row reordering, tree data, and virtualization (demo: 31 columns × 100,000 rows). **DataGridPremium** adds row grouping with aggregation and Excel export.
- Also in MUI X: **Charts**, **Date/Time Pickers**, **Tree View**.

### Not published
A canonical total component count is not published; coverage is enumerated by category on the all-components page.
sections.dataviz:
### Data Visualization
> Source: https://mui.com/x/react-charts/

**MUI X Charts** (`@mui/x-charts`) is a collection of SVG-rendered React chart components with D3-based data manipulation, themeable via the MUI theme and composable from building blocks (`ChartsDataProvider`, `ChartSurface`, `BarPlot`, `ChartsXAxis`, etc.).

### Chart types
| Chart | Tier |
| --- | --- |
| Bar Chart | Community |
| Line Chart | Community |
| Area Chart | Community |
| Pie (Donut) Chart | Community |
| Scatter Chart | Community |
| Sparkline | Community |
| Gauge | Community |
| Radar Chart | Community |
| Range Bar Chart | Community |
| Heatmap | Pro |
| Funnel Chart | Pro |
| Pyramid Chart | Pro |
| Sankey Chart | Pro |
| Candlestick / OHLC | Premium |

### Shared features
Axes, legends, labels, stacking, styling, tooltips, highlighting, zoom & pan, and export are shared across chart components. Premium adds WebGL rendering for dense datasets. **Planned:** Treemap, Gantt Chart.

### Licensing
Open-core: Community is MIT (core chart types + building blocks); Pro adds advanced charts and interactions (zoom, pan, export); Premium adds WebGL performance and financial charts.
sections.content:
### Content: Voice & Tone
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/all-components/

### Not published
MUI is a UI component library and does not define a voice-and-tone, microcopy, or content-writing standard. Component pages document APIs, usage, and accessibility, but no editorial/content guidelines are published. (Material Design's own content guidance lives in Google's Material system, not in MUI's documentation.)
sections.accessibility:
### Accessibility
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/react-button/ · https://mui.com/material-ui/react-link/ · https://v6.mui.com/base-ui/getting-started/accessibility/

MUI components follow the **WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices (APG)** to provide keyboard accessibility and correct roles out of the box. Each component page links the relevant W3C APG pattern via a `waiAria` reference (e.g. Button → APG Button pattern, Link → APG Link pattern) and documents keyboard interaction, focus, and ARIA requirements.

### Documented behaviors
- **Keyboard navigation**: interactive components are Tab-focusable; list-like components (Select, Menu) support arrow keys, Home, End, Enter, Esc, and alphanumeric type-ahead.
- **Focus indication**: `.Mui-focusVisible` state class marks keyboard focus; developers must ensure a visible `:focus-visible` style (per WCAG focus-appearance guidance).
- **Accessible names**: form controls need an associated `label`/`aria-label`; icon-only buttons require `aria-label`.
- **Contrast**: set `palette.contrastThreshold: 4.5` to target WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (4.5:1). An `enhanceHighContrast` theme enhancer (v9.1.0+) adds Windows High Contrast / forced-colors overrides.
- **Base UI** primitives adhere to WAI-ARIA 1.2 and are tested with NVDA, JAWS, and VoiceOver.

### Known gaps
MUI states the library "cannot make your application fully accessible on its own" — developers remain responsible for focus indication, accessible names, and correct ARIA when customizing components. Accessibility is documented per component rather than as one central conformance report.
sections.dosdonts:
### Do's and Don'ts
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/palette/ · https://mui.com/material-ui/react-link/

Guidance is embedded per component and in the customization guides rather than in a single rulebook.

### Do
- **Do** customize through the `theme` (palette, typography, spacing, shape) so changes cascade consistently.
- **Do** provide only `main` for a custom palette color and let `light`/`dark`/`contrastText` be derived (or set `contrastThreshold: 4.5` for WCAG contrast).
- **Do** give links specific, descriptive text (avoid "click here"); add `aria-label` when a link opens a new window.
- **Do** keep accessible names and keyboard behavior when customizing components.

### Don't
- **Don't** strip ARIA roles or keyboard handling when restyling (e.g. re-implementing a Button as a bare `div`).
- **Don't** hardcode values that a theme token already supplies — use `theme.spacing()`, `theme.shape.borderRadius`, and palette tokens.

### Not published
There is no shipped design linter; guardrails come from the theme, TypeScript prop types, and per-component usage guidance rather than an automated do/don't checker.
sections.agent:
### Agent Guidance & Delivery
> Source: https://mui.com/material-ui/getting-started/mcp/

### Official MCP server
MUI publishes an official **Model Context Protocol** server, **`@mui/mcp`**, run locally over the `stdio` transport (`npx -y @mui/mcp@latest`). Setup instructions are provided for VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, JetBrains, Zed, and Claude Code (`claude mcp add mui-mcp -- npx -y @mui/mcp@latest`). It exposes tools such as `useMuiDocs` (fetch package docs) and `fetchDocs` (fetch additional docs by returned URL) so agents can quote real sources and avoid hallucinated links.

### LLM-legible docs delivery
- Every documentation page has a **Markdown counterpart** at a `.md` URL (e.g. `https://mui.com/material-ui/react-button.md`), giving agents clean, parseable content including `waiAria`, `githubSource`, and API tables.
- Extensive TypeScript types make component props agent-legible.
- MUI recommends adding an editor rule instructing the assistant to call `useMuiDocs` → `fetchDocs` iteratively before answering.

### Not published / not verified
A root **`llms.txt`** at `https://mui.com/llms.txt` returns **404** (not published); LLM delivery is via the official MCP server plus per-page `.md` documents rather than an `llms.txt` index.
